comments.note: A04 — Insecure Design (Low): The GET /api/notes handler (src/server/routes/notes.ts) has no try/catch around the projectManager.list() / workspaceManager.list() calls. If either throws (e.g. on storage corruption), the router's catch block captures the error but sends no HTTP response — the client connection hangs. All other route handlers in the codebase (e.g. workspaces.ts) wrap manager calls in try/catch and return a 500. Recommendation: wrap the handler body in a try/catch and send sendError(res, 500, 'Internal server error.') on failure, consistent with the established pattern.

A01 — Broken Access Control (Info): GET /api/notes returns ALL projects and ALL workspace notes in a single unauthenticated response. This is consistent with the local-only, single-user design of the tool. If the tool is ever deployed in a networked or multi-tenant context, this endpoint would require scoped access control. No action required at this stage.

No other security findings — all OWASP Top 10 categories reviewed. No new dependencies introduced. GET /api/notes reads only from the in-memory/storage-backed managers and returns JSON via sendJson (JSON.stringify). No user-controlled input is processed in this endpoint. No injection vectors, no secrets exposed, no stack traces in responses, no SSRF. Notes values returned as-is from storage (frontend must escape when rendering, but that is outside this WP scope).

summary: Code review FAIL. One blocking issue: src/server/routes/notes.ts GET /api/notes handler has no try/catch. The Router is designed such that handlers own their error responses (documented in router.ts). On any storage error the connection hangs with no HTTP response. Every other handler in the codebase wraps manager calls in try/catch and returns a 500. This must be fixed before PASS can be given.

comments.note: BLOCKING: src/server/routes/notes.ts registerNotesRoutes() handler lacks a try/catch around the projectManager.list() and workspaceManager.list() calls. The Router's own documentation explicitly states: 'Handlers are responsible for writing their own error responses — the router does not send an additional one.' When the router's .catch() fires it only logs the error; it does NOT send an HTTP response. This means any storage-level error (file I/O failure, JSON parse error on the project file, etc.) causes the client connection to hang with no response until it times out. Every other route handler in the codebase (e.g. workspaces.ts GET /list, GET /:wid, PUT /:wid, POST /setup, etc.) wraps manager calls in try/catch and returns sendError(res, 500, ...) on failure. The fix is to wrap the handler body in try/catch and call sendError(res, 500, 'Internal server error.') in the catch clause, consistent with the established codebase pattern. A test for this error path should also be added.
